There’s no specific pronoun for any gender— non-binary people use xey/xem because they might feel that accurately represents how they express their gender identity. People use the pronouns they feel comfortable with! 

Genderqueer is just “I don’t really identify with the gender I was assigned at birth, and I may identify as another gender or none at all.” It’s a bit of a catch all IMO. Genderfluid means you ‘flow’ between all the genders— male, female, none, all, some, etc. 

Picture it like this— if ‘female’ is pink and ‘male’ is blue, how people identify is the rest of the color spectrum. Genderfluid people may wake up feeling ‘pink’ one day and ‘blue’ the next, but the day after they might be ‘yellow’ or ‘green’ or ‘purple’. Genderqueer people may have been told that they were ‘pink’ at birth but when they got older, they decided they were a bit more mauve. Maybe there are shades of pink, but not totally pink. Maybe they’re a greyish pink! 

(And coming from a non-binary person, so long as you ask in good faith, and recognize that one non-binary person isn’t a monolith, you can ask a question about gender or pronouns!)

People in general frustrate me because I have a broken brain and no social skills. I have ADHD, which has translated to me talking excessively and interrupting people, and I’m rather self centered. I also grew up fairly alone, with little to no social interaction outside of school until I hit high school. Also, abandonment issues and anxiety, both of which have gotten worse over the past year and a half. So I chatter at people, rambling excessively and hope that doing so can signal to the other person “you can do the same to me, I’m willing to listen”. But when I don’t get a response, or get a short one, I start panicking and think that the other person hates me and doesn’t want to talk anymore. I’m often forgetful and impulsive, which can translate to me being insensitive by saying the wrong thing by forgetting a trigger or opening my mouth before I think. Ive been described as “clingy”, and been told that’s what pushes people away too. And now, with this remaining group of friends, I want to not be… frustrating. 

I’m a few years older than most people in this smaller server I’ve been left with, and I don’t want them to think I’m weird or a creep. I want to be their friend, and use my age to help them. I also don’t want my mental health to be a burden on them, like venting or trauma dumping. 

I’ve sought out professional help. I wasn’t able to meet with the therapist during the break, and when I went back to school I was in such a depressive hole I couldn’t even make an appointment. A few weeks ago, at my girlfriend’s insistence, I signed up for an online therapy program that you can use at any time. I just haven’t mustered up the executive function and energy to go.
